_comment: Module-level graded competencies — one entry per skill named in module_decks/*/PROJECT.md's competency_assessments list. `definition` is hand-written in plain, student-readable language, informed by (but not pasted from) each module's INSTRUCTOR_MODULE_SUMMARY.md rubric table ('Rubric ceiling' + 'Assessment method' columns — instructor-facing rubric shorthand, not something to show students directly). See extract_skills.py's header for the regeneration workflow when a new deck lands: it writes skills_raw.json (the raw ceiling/method text) as a reference; this file itself is maintained by hand on top of that. `modules` is for traceability only — never surface a module name in a reading's visible text.

general-programming-coding.name: General Programming & Coding
general-programming-coding.definition: Recognizing and labeling basic programming concepts and terminal commands in context, even before writing original code from scratch.

data-literacy.name: Data Literacy
data-literacy.definition: Independently inspecting a real dataset and drawing accurate, well-reasoned conclusions about what it does and doesn't tell you.

git-version-control.name: Git & Version Control
git-version-control.definition: Using Git and GitHub to track, commit, and share your own work in a real repository, following expected conventions.

ai-literacy.name: AI Literacy
ai-literacy.definition: Using an AI tool thoughtfully, and being able to explain in writing what it got right, what it missed, and how you verified its answer.

curiosity.name: Curiosity
curiosity.definition: Following up on an unexpected or interesting detail in your work with a genuine question or further investigation, not just moving past it.

critical-thinking.name: Critical Thinking
critical-thinking.definition: Questioning an assumption, a data source, or an AI-generated answer, and backing that judgment up with specific reasoning rather than a gut feeling.

terminal-command-line.name: Terminal & Command Line
terminal-command-line.definition: Navigating a computer's file system and running real commands from the terminal, not just clicking through a graphical interface.

control-flow-loops.name: Control Flow & Loops
control-flow-loops.definition: Tracing exactly what a loop or a conditional will do step by step, and comparing two different working approaches to the same repeated task.

functions-modular-programming.name: Functions & Modular Programming
functions-modular-programming.definition: Breaking a program into well-scoped, reusable functions instead of one long block, and independently debugging code organized that way.

object-oriented-programming.name: Object-Oriented Programming
object-oriented-programming.definition: Designing a class with the right attributes and methods for a real problem, and explaining how its objects behave independently of each other.

algorithmic-complexity-big-o.name: Algorithmic Complexity (Big-O)
algorithmic-complexity-big-o.definition: Comparing two approaches to the same problem by how their cost grows as the amount of data grows, backed by your own code or example, not just naming the pattern from memory.

attention-to-detail.name: Attention to Detail
attention-to-detail.definition: Independently catching a planted bug, edge case, or inconsistency that a surface-level read-through would miss.

statistical-analysis.name: Statistical Analysis
statistical-analysis.definition: Interpreting summary statistics like mean, median, and standard deviation against what they actually mean for a real business or real-world question.

data-distributions-shape.name: Data Distributions & Shape
data-distributions-shape.definition: Reading the shape of a real distribution (skew, outliers, spread) across multiple variables and matching it to the right chart or summary.

data-mining.name: Data Mining
data-mining.definition: Digging into a real dataset to surface a genuinely non-obvious relationship or finding, not just restating what's already visible on the surface.

data-cleaning-imputation.name: Data Cleaning & Imputation
data-cleaning-imputation.definition: Writing a real, reusable function to clean messy data and making a justified, documented decision about how to handle missing values.

stakeholder-communication.name: Stakeholder Communication
stakeholder-communication.definition: Writing up findings for a real audience who wasn't in the room for the analysis, with a clear structure and an actual supporting visual.

sql.name: SQL
sql.definition: Writing correct, verified SQL against a real database: joins, GROUP BY/HAVING, CTEs, window functions, and reading a query's real execution plan.

relational-databases.name: Relational Databases
relational-databases.definition: Designing correct primary/foreign keys that express real relationships, normalized appropriately, and identifying a genuine design flaw in an existing schema.

database-administration.name: Database Administration
database-administration.definition: Creating a real database and tables from the command line with correct types and constraints, including setting up and testing access permissions.

data-modeling.name: Data Modeling
data-modeling.definition: Mapping real business questions to a database schema before writing any code, with normalization and constraint choices you can explain and defend.
